claim_register.claim_scope:
The WIP guide covers implementation and developer-maintained tests in RATAN Java repositories.
It SHOULD serve as a code-review reference and does not cover every concern.
It uses RFC 2119 obligation terms.
Its bibliography supplies references, without adding independently reviewed rules.

claim_register.claim_scope:
Package names SHOULD use lower_snake_case.
Method, parameter, member, and local names MUST use lowerCamelCase.
Constants and enums MUST use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; type parameters MUST use one capital letter.
Constants MUST NOT omit final.
The guide distinguishes deep immutable constants from arbitrary static-final fields.
It describes unused imports, raw JSON maps, and raw generic types as review concerns.
OOP principles SHOULD guide design.
Members MUST use the most restrictive access that makes sense, normally private.
claim_register.rationale: The selected original passages explicitly describe this historical design, condition, or proposal.

claim_register.claim_scope:
Cyclomatic complexity SHOULD not exceed 10; cognitive complexity SHOULD be less than 15.
Parameter types SHOULD protect encapsulation.
The guide recommends combining OOP and functional style and minimizing side effects.
Its example separates validation failure through an exception instead of mutating the returned object.
claim_register.rationale: The selected original passages explicitly describe this historical design, condition, or proposal.

claim_register.claim_scope:
Generally available JDK17 features MAY be used; preview and experimental features MUST NOT be used.
The guide calls for removing unused methods, variables, and assignments.
Debug code MUST NOT enter production.
Constructor injection SHOULD replace field injection.
It prefers text blocks for multiline strings.
XML generation SHOULD use a Java-bean XML library instead of a template engine.
claim_register.rationale: The selected original passages explicitly describe this historical design, condition, or proposal.

claim_register.claim_scope:
Stream.toList() SHOULD be used when an unmodifiable list is required.
The guide prefers isEmpty for collection emptiness checks.
InterruptedException needs rethrowing or restoration of the interrupt flag; logging alone is insufficient.
Resources require release on every path.
Try-with-resources SHOULD close resources; locks SHOULD unlock in finally.
The database rule MUST update the timestamp when saving.
Its prose names update_at, while its example uses updated_at; the exact column contract needs confirmation.
claim_register.rationale: The selected original passages explicitly describe this historical design, condition, or proposal.

claim_register.claim_scope:
Generated noise comments SHOULD NOT be enabled; Git SHOULD supply creator history.
Commented-out code MUST NOT remain.
The guide allows disabled-test annotations when a justified test must remain; it does not grant release acceptance.
Unclear code SHOULD be refactored or explained.
Common business logic belongs in ADO with commit traceability.
Deprecated code SHOULD use @Deprecated and MUST explain the reason and alternative.
Incoming requests MUST be logged unless justified otherwise; external API requests and responses MUST be logged.
Large fields MUST NOT be logged.
Placeholders SHOULD replace concatenation, and log markers SHOULD use business descriptions.
The excerpt does not define sensitive-data redaction or retention policy.
claim_register.rationale: The selected original passages explicitly describe this historical design, condition, or proposal.

claim_register.claim_scope:
Each Java class SHOULD have a corresponding test; classes without logic are listed as exceptions.
Tests MUST follow FIRST and Given-When-Then; When and Then are mandatory.
Tests MUST contain enough assertions to check behavior and relevant fields.
Printing or checking only non-null is insufficient for the shown field-producing example.
Test-only main methods MUST NOT be added.
Each test should cover one scenario.
Unit tests MUST mock external dependencies and run without a real database or external API.

That discrepancy remains unresolved.
JUnit5 tests should generally have package visibility.
Bug fixes MUST make the best effort to cover missed cases.
The examples are illustrative and were not executed in this review.
